source_text: Si ergo et Manichaeus non ob aliud dicit malam naturam, quam quod eam mali meriti arbitratur, cui putat inferenda supplicia, et tu naturae humanae malum inesse confirmas nec aliud malum quam quod Manichaeus, id est concupiscentiam carnis, quam a diabolo contionaris infusam; eamque sic mali meriti esse dicis, ut aeternis eam persistas adiudicare tormentis, non aliter sine dubio quam Manichaeus pessimam illam damnatamque pronuntias.
pass_a_gloss: If therefore also the Manichaean says an evil nature not for another reason than that he judges it of evil desert, to which he thinks punishments must be inflicted, and you confirm evil is in human nature nor another evil than what the Manichaean, that is the desire of the flesh, which you orate infused by the devil; and you say it is of so evil desert that you persist to adjudge it to eternal torments, not otherwise without doubt than the Manichaean you pronounce that most bad and condemned.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS concupiscentia=eager desire; Blaise Christian usage often sexual desire vs nuptiae
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS meritum; Blaise; avoid later merit-theology

pass_b_english: Mani calls nature evil for no other reason than that he considers it deserving of evil, and thinks punishments should be inflicted on it. You also affirm evil exists in human nature, and no different evil from Mani’s: fleshly desire, which you publicly proclaim was poured in by the devil. You say nature is so deserving of evil that you persist in sentencing it to eternal torments. Without doubt, then, you pronounce it utterly evil and condemned in exactly the same way as Mani.

choices.why: Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.
Julian distinguishes nuptiae from concupiscentia; do not flatten to 'lust' as a nature-sin substance.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
